title: Number of Women in National Congress Sees Sharp Rise
seoTitle: More Women Elected to Brazil's Congress
subtitle: The female caucus in the Chamber of Deputies reaches 109 representatives, a 21% increase
excerpt: Female representation in the Chamber of Deputies rose from 90 to 109 lawmakers, marking the largest female caucus in history.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The female caucus in the Chamber of Deputies and the Federal Senate has reached its highest number on record. In the Chamber, the total number of elected women reached 109, representing a 21% growth compared to the previous figure of 90.

Impact of the increase

This numerical jump indicates a shift in the composition of the Legislature, expanding the presence of female voices in discussions and decisions that affect Brazilian society.

Institutional context

Caucuses are formed by lawmakers elected by each state and the Federal District, who come together to coordinate actions and positions within the legislative houses. The expansion of the female caucus reflects the growing participation of women in electoral processes and political representation.

With information from Agência Brasil.
